To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
grassland species richness is mainly determined by ecological and topographic variables, with a secondary effect of management practices, while the landscape configuration is of minor relevance.

(i) the abandonment of agro-pasture practices has caused the decline of semi-natural grasslands in both study areas; (ii) the reduction of grassland patches was higher in the eastern valley; (iii) the main drivers of grassland species richness are related to topographic, management, ecological factors and only to a lesser extent to landscape factors.
the decline in grassland patches in the two alpine valleys was mainly caused by the abandonment of traditional agro-pastorals practices.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a detailed analysis of the effect of land cover changes on the conservation of plant biodiversity in alpine valleys.

the role of landscape configuration on grassland patch diversity, but also with the effect of land use on grassland species richness and the role of ecological factors on grassland patch conservation.
the importance of ecological and topographic features in determining the current plant species richness of alpine grassland patches.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the abandonment process is a major factor in the reduction of grassland area and species richness, but it is not the only one.

, in the Alps, grassland patch conservation is strongly dependent on local management practices, which are influenced by historical and current land-use changes, and by local topographic and ecological factors, which can affect the intensity and type of management.
, in the two alpine valleys studied, grassland patch diversity was more influenced by ecological, topographic factors and management intensity than by landscape features.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the most relevant factors for the maintenance of grassland plant diversity are related to the ecological conditions of the patches, the topographic features, and the management intensity, which should be taken into account when designing conservation strategies.
the conservation of grassland patches is not only related to their area, but also to their management and to the surrounding landscape.
the loss of grassland patches in the Alps is not only a matter of landscape fragmentation, but also of a loss of traditional land use, with a consequent reduction of plant diversity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the management of the surrounding matrix and the landscape configuration are of primary importance for grassland conservation.
, to preserve the biodiversity of grasslands, the conservation of traditional land uses is crucial.
the abandonment process of grasslands in the Alps has been different across valleys.
